plain.text: Joseph had his steward fill the brothers' sacks with food, return their silver, and put his own silver cup in Benjamin's sack. When they had gone a short way, the steward caught up and accused them of stealing the cup. They were sure of their innocence and said whoever had it would die and the rest would become slaves. The cup was found in Benjamin's sack. They tore their clothes and returned to the city. Judah and his brothers threw themselves to the ground before Joseph. Judah said, "God has uncovered your servants' guilt. We are now your slaves." Joseph said only the man with the cup would be his slave; the rest could go home in peace.

Judah came near and pleaded. He told how their father had lost one son already and loved Benjamin dearly. Their father had said that if harm came to Benjamin, they would bring his grey head down to the grave in sorrow. Judah had guaranteed the boy's safety. "Now please let your servant remain here as my lord's slave in place of the boy, and let the boy return with his brothers. How can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I could not bear to see the misery that would come on my father."

summary.bigIdea: Judah, who once sold Joseph, offers to become a slave in Benjamin's place to spare his father more grief.
points: Joseph tests his brothers by planting his cup in Benjamin's sack.
The brothers refuse to abandon Benjamin and return together.
Judah offers his own life as a slave instead of Benjamin.
summary.reflection: Judah offered to take Benjamin's place. Where do you see self-giving love like this in the Bible or in life?
